ops.body:
Approved 2026-07-25; **corrected 2026-07-27 against wave-1 measurements**, several of which refuted the original reasoning. Decisions fixed up front: note `acd2aac`. Measured refutations: notes `3628756` (concept extraction) and `87ea946` (spawnllm).

## The problem

cc-notes accumulates a typed record across every branch and almost none is retrievable. Measured in `~/Code/monorepo`: 94 entities, 343 fold ops, 1,617 remote branches. Fleet-wide: ~775 entities across 11 repos. `cc-notes search "rust build"` returns zero results; `cc-notes relevant go` returns one already-drifted doc.

1. **Relevance is substring matching.** `textTier` (`notes/document.go:637`) scores title-contains 3, tag 2, body 1, else 0. Case-insensitive `strings.Contains` is the whole relevance function.
2. **The task layer is disconnected from code.** No note→note, note→task or doc→task reference field exists. `Criterion.Note` and `Finding.Note` are free-form evidence strings, not entity references (`model/model.go:333,347`).
3. **Edges that exist are written but not read.** A 40-row audit found 9 dead, 26 partially wired, 4 fully wired.

## What wave 1 actually measured — read this before trusting the design

**The bar is BM25 at NDCG@10 0.805**, not the naive control. Run for real through `internal/kg/eval` over 42 monorepo questions, 5 seeds: BM25 ndcg 0.805 / recall 0.910 / mrr 0.789 / leak 0.100 / abstain 0.000; full-context control 0.054. **`factual` questions are already at 0.972 — lexical retrieval is not the weak part.** The headroom is `cross_branch` 0.596 (with recall 0.929: BM25 *finds* the records and *ranks* them badly), `staleness` 0.564, `multihop` 0.741, a 0.100 superseded-leak rate, and total inability to abstain at any fixed threshold. **This is precisely the "ranking, staleness and cross-branch reach — not recall" reframe, now measured rather than argued.**

**The connectivity premise was wrong (note `3628756`).** The graph is already connected — 4 components, 94% of the monorepo in the largest, median degree 20. Component count is a worthless objective; the target is same-topic pair F1, whose measured ladder is baseline .57 → +regex .68. "Most notes are untagged" was false and named the wrong kind: **tasks** are the untagged kind (59%) and carry **zero anchors, 290 of 290**, so anchors contribute no note↔task edges corpus-wide.

**Concept extraction is a regex, not a model.** A 289M GLiNER encoder lost to an identifier regex on the only spans that create edges (37% vs 67% precision at df≥2) while costing 2001 s against 0.2 s. Cut. The regex needs a document-frequency cap (42% of its raw edge mass is each repo's own name) and a bare-version filter.

**The free signal nobody uses is the per-op `session` id** — F1 .48 standalone, above tags (.38) and above the raw regex (.45).

**Dense retrieval never beats BM25 alone.** RRF fusion wins only on conceptual paraphrase (+0.181 NDCG, p=0.002); dense-only loses everywhere. Dense must embed **title+tags, not the body** (0.238 vs 0.180 pooled conceptual — static mean-pooling dilutes with length). `potion-base-8M` is correct; bigger pins add nothing measurable. **Owner decision 2026-07-27: hold the dense lane built but unshipped** until the graph, staleness gating and abstention are measured — the headroom above is not where dense helps.

**The daemon's value case is real but was justified by the wrong number.** The wasm compile is *not* the cost — wazero's on-disk AOT cache already amortizes it across processes (996 → 21 ms) and ships today. The cost is `em_load_model` at **133 ms, 79% of warm engine init**, which only a resident process can amortize. Per call 209 → 11 ms. Two corrections: the **exec floor does not vanish** (of the 11 ms, only 2.6 ms is the daemon — the client MUST be a small purpose-built binary, never the 25 MB one), and a daemon holding the engine costs **~435 MB permanently resident**.

**spawnllm's Go binding is pure Go, no cgo** (note `87ea946`) — but `map_concurrent` does not exist there, `openai_endpoint` *is* reachable and is the only in-process lane, and "direct Go binding" still means a subprocess per provider call. Route enrichment to codex: 4.5 s vs claude's 38.6 s for the same work.

**Three MCP tool guards exist, not two.** `redirect_inventory_test.go:71` machine-enforces `CC_NOTES_TOOLS` in both directions and has since 2026-07-16. Planning material claiming the pack is hand-mirrored is wrong.

**`EvalSymlinks` is mandatory, and more urgently than assumed.** A repo and its own linked worktree already produce different raw keys on macOS with no deliberate symlink, because git returns `/private/var` for one and lexical `/var` for the other. Use **32 hex chars**, not 16 — the key names a directory that would hold another repo's data on collision. `gitcmd.Dirs` succeeds silently on a bare repo.

## Phases

- **T** — threading, lands first. T1/T2 shipped (`f62eca0`): nine reverse-index methods consolidated, `dto.go` the single projection, `superseded_by` array truncation fixed, blockers from one indexed pass (measured 106× faster than per-row at N=160). T3 adds writers plus **first-class task anchors** (owner decision: real anchors AND a graph-side backfill from `Commits []SHA`, marked derived). T4 the open-findings gate. T5 status. T6 hooks write edges. T7 tasks in the search corpus. **`notes/relevant.go` is FROZEN** — every change anyone would propose there *is* the ranker.
- **0** — the embedding module, built and green in a cc-context worktree, **held unshipped**. Nested module `github.com/yasyf/cc-context/semsearch`; surface is wazero + `x/sys` only. Blocked on a human uploading the wasm to a new HF repo, deliberately not done.
- **D** — one global unsigned daemonkit service. Never a second agent in the signed helper's plan: `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` is on `ForbiddenInjectionEntitlements` and CI hard-fails any entitlement key, so wazero's compiler is categorically forbidden there.
- **1** — the graph builder, zero LLM. Reuses `fold.History` → `trail.Entries` and `viz.classify`'s 16-verb vocabulary. Now also owns the session edge and the regex concept lane, both moved out of Phase 6 because neither needs a model.
- **2** — retrieval. Start from `internal/web/fusion.go`, not `rank/fusion.go`: the latter's boost and penalty stacks are all code-specific and wrong for prose. The PPR kill test is real.
- **3** — staleness S1–S9 on the existing `Verdict` machinery. Two measured targets: drive leak 0.100 → ~0, and build an abstention mechanism BM25 structurally cannot provide.
- **4** — injection. Three tiers already ship; swap the payload, add the pre-action gate.
- **5** — the eval. Shipped and running: 52 questions from real history, superseded-leak and abstention metrics, ≥5 seeds.
- **6** — the async LLM lane, gated on 5, now much smaller: salience scoring, conflict adjudication, injection compression. The extraction half moved to Phase 1.

## What the literature settled

74 systems surveyed. Adopt: two layers (append-only episodic truth + a rebuildable derived layer); LLM-free retrieval; RRF fusion; invalidate-never-delete; importance scored once at write time; decay keyed to last verify; Aider's zero-LLM personalized PageRank; a deterministic pre-action gate.

Cut on evidence: community detection (our corpus is ~200k tokens — there is no corpus-scale sensemaking problem); 4-timestamp bitemporal edges (fold checkpoint replay already *is* that guarantee); embedded graph/vector DBs and ANN (sqlite-vec is cgo, Kuzu is cgo and archived; brute-force cosine is <2 ms here).

**The governing economics:** injecting 1,500 tokens at session start costs ~$4.50/mo at 20 sessions/day — 22× the entire hosted-tiny ingestion budget. Injected tokens cost more than producing them, so every design dollar belongs in precision.

**The skeptic's case, which wave 1 partly vindicated:** Mem0's own paper shows a full-context baseline (J=72.90%) beating Mem0 (66.88%). Letta's plain filesystem agent scored 74.0% on LoCoMo vs Mem0's 68.5%. Zep's 84% headline came from an arithmetic error. GraphRAG-Bench found community-based global search *underperforms* standard RAG. Here the naive control scored 0.054 — but BM25 scored 0.805, and **BM25, not the control, is the baseline that matters.**
